takeaway: Superior gluteal nerve injury paralyses gluteus medius, minimus and tensor fascia lata, giving a positive Trendelenburg test.

question.text: A 74-year-old woman has a positive Trendelenburg test after a hip replacement. Injury to which nerve is the most likely explanation?

lines.text: After her hip replacement, this lady has a positive Trendelenburg test.
The superior gluteal nerve supplies three muscles: gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fascia lata.
When this nerve is injured, all three are paralysed.
Normally, gluteus medius tilts the pelvis to lift the opposite side as we walk.
Without it, gravity wins and the unsupported hip drops, giving a lurching gait.
So the answer is the superior gluteal nerve.
